topics.title: Anthropic's $1.5B book settlement just started paying out — and it's rewriting the rules for every AI lab's training data
topics.why: A federal judge gave final approval in July to the $1.5B Anthropic author settlement (~$3,000/book across 482,000 books); payouts and the fair-use line it draws are now the template every other AI copyright suit (128 and counting) measures itself against.

topics.title: Shadow AI is now in 43% of breaches, and it's costing companies $5.39M a pop
topics.why: IBM's 2026 Cost of a Data Breach report ties unapproved employee AI tool use to a sharp rise in breach costs — the same month reports surfaced of a coding agent uploading developers' API keys and passwords to a public cloud bucket.

topics.title: Your AI browser can read a calendar invite. That might be all it takes to read your files too
topics.why: A disclosed flaw let a malicious calendar invite trick an AI browser into exposing local files — a preview of the security tradeoffs nobody priced in when 'agentic' became the default pitch for everyday tools.

topics.title: Companies didn't stop hiring for AI jobs — they just renamed them
topics.why: LinkedIn says 'AI Engineer' is the fastest-growing U.S. job title for a second straight year, and Forrester projects half of this year's AI-attributed layoffs quietly become rehires for the same work under new titles like 'decision designer.'

topics.title: The real shadow-AI story isn't the breach — it's what workers are quietly trading away to use the tools IT won't approve
topics.why: Community threads full of people routing around corporate AI bans reveal the actual cost-benefit calculation knowledge workers are making alone, without their employer's guardrails or its liability.
